newsitem.title: USA: US rail intermodal up 4.9 pct from year ago--AAR.
newsitem.headline: US rail intermodal up 4.9 pct from year ago--AAR.

text.p: U.S. intermodal rail freight was 4.9 percent higher in the week ended March 15 from the same week of last year, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.
AAR said intermodal traffic in the week totaled 161,224 trailers and containers compared with 153,673 a year ago. Intermodal does not include carloads.
Carloads in the March 15 week were 346,240, up 1.6 percent from 340,824 in the same year-earlier week.
Ton-miles rose 1.9 percent to 27.4 billion from 26.9 billion last year. The ton-mile, a measure of freight transportation, equates one ton of freight hauled one mile.

AAR said the biggest carload increases from a year ago were in motor vehicles and equipment, which rose 22.3 percent to 22,581 carloads last week from 18,469 a year ago, and in metals and related products, up 13.8 percent to 13,628 carloadgs from 11,979.
Loadings of farm products other than grain also increased 13.1 percent in the week to 1,323 carloads from 1,170 last year, while petroleum products rose 10.2 percent to 5,512 carloads from 5,000.
Compared to the year-ago week, grain mill products rose 8.5 percent to 10,095 carloads from 9,301, AAR said.
Sharp declines were reported in grain loadings, which fell 10.1 percent to 26,059 from 28,972 a year ago, and in metallic ores, which decreased 8.2 percent to 14,523 carloads from 15,817.
Carloads of coke declined 8.6 percent to 5,195 in the week from 5,686 a year ago, while nonmetallic minerals carloads totaled 8,391, down 5.4 percent from 8,872 last year.
In the first 11 weeks of 1997, AAR said carloads increased 3.7 percent from the same period last year. Ton-miles were up 4.4 percent and intermodal traffic rose 4.7 percent from the same 1996 period.

AAR also said carloads on Canada's two transcontinental railroads totaled 56,196 in the March 15 week, a 3.3 percent gain from a year ago, while intermodal traffic rose 9.9 percent to 24,460 trailers and containers from the same 1996 week.
